FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard (Part VII) (Seconu Revision) was adopted

by the Indian Standards Institution on 17 May 1972. after the draft
finalized by the CivH Works Measurement Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 1.2 Measurement occupies a very important place in the planning and execution of any civil engineering work from the time of first estimates to the final completion anel settlement of payments for a project. Methods followed rut measurement are not uniCornl and considerable differences exist between practices followed by different construction agencies and also between various Central and State Government Departments. While it i. recognized that each system of measurement has t() be speci. fically related to administrative and financial organizations within a department responsible for the work, a unification of various systems at technical level haa been accepted as very desirable specially as it permits a wider range of operatitn for civil engineering contractors and eliminates ambiguities and misunddrStandings of various systems followed. 0.3 Among various civil engineering items, measurement of buildinga was the fint to be taken up for standardization and this standard h~vinl pro-

visions relating to building work was fint published in 1958' anCl was revised in 1964. 8.ti In the course of usage of this standard by various construction agencies in the country, several clarifications and suggestions for modifications were received and as a result of study, the technical committee responsible for this standard decided to cover method of measurement for civil engineering works like industrial and river valley projects.
0.5 For the pu~e of deciding whether a particular requirement of this ,tandard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expres~ng the resUlt a meuureJnent. shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2�1960�. The number ofsignificant places retained in the rounded oft'value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard�

or

1.1 This standard (Part VII) coven the method of measurement of hardware in buildings and civil -engineering works.

2.GBNERAL
2.1 ne.c:rIpdOD 01 lum - The description of each item shall, unless
otherwise stated, be held to include, wherever necessary, conveyance and delivery, handling, unloading, storing and all labour for fitting and fixing in poaition t cutting and waste, return of packing, etc.

2.2 LImJt. 01 Meu....m ��t - The dimensioDi shall be measured net in decimal system nearest to 0-01 m,
~.3 BID. 01 Q, . . .dd. - The bills of quantities shall fully describe the materials and workmanship and accurately represent the work to be

executed.

2.4 Mode df M.8aremeDt. - The various kinds of builders hardware shall be described and measured separately according to the material, finish, size, pattern and method offixing. 2.4.1 All builden hardware shall be fully described and enumerated except the following which mall be measured in running metres: a) Curtain roda or poles, stating the outer diameter; b) Curtain Raila - Curtain runnen, brackets and stops shall be described and included with the item Itating the number per metre of rail; c) Rails for .liding luhes stating the size of the rail j and d) Suh Linea - The girth or diameter thall be ltated. 2.5 Fixing of hardware items ahaIl include aU fittings, cutting, ainkm" boring and momcing, the supply of screws ( or bolts, nuts and waahen In the case of hardware made for fixing with bolts), to match.

2.& Hardware fixeel to wood and metal ahall each be meuured aeparately.
2.7 Hardware fixed Bush shall be 80 delClibed.
